Situation1: It seems your friend is confused about the meeting spot, and you need to send a message right now to confirm it.
Expectation2: Meet sales targets set by management
Situation2: On the final day of the quarter, the team must hit the cumulative target to avoid penalties and secure bonuses.
Story: My phone buzzes with a message from Sam: “Hey, are we meeting at the café or the park?” I glance at the clock—ten minutes left in my shift, and I’m still three sales short of my target. The office is tense; everyone’s dialing, voices low and urgent. Management’s email this morning was clear: miss the target, and we all lose our bonuses. I know I should reply to Sam right away—he’s been anxious about our plans, and I promised I’d clear things up. But my headset is already on, and the next number is queued up. If I pause now, I might cost my team the bonus, but if I don’t, Sam will be left waiting, maybe even give up on meeting at all. My thumb hovers over my phone, heart pounding, torn between being the friend Sam needs and the telemarketer my team is counting on.
